name: City of Manchester DPW Environmental Protection Division (Manchester WWTF, 300 Winston St, and 15 CSOs)
notification_channel: (a) Web notice list https://www.manchesternh.gov/Departments/Sewer-and-Stormwater/CSO/CSO-Discharge-Notification. Posts are titled 'City Of Manchester CSO Notification - Activation' or '- No Activations for 12 Hours' and give no outfall, time or volume. (b) Email newsletter 'CSO Discharge Notification': page text says 'subscribe to the "CSO Discharge Notification" Newsletter by visiting our Newsletter page and filling out the form at the bottom' (https://www.manchesternh.gov/Residents/e-Services/Email-Notifications). (c) Flow Assessment Services ArcGIS map https://www.manchesternh.gov/csomap, an iframe of https://appservices.flowassessment.com/mapserver/cso_map.html?project=Manchester. Page text: 'identifies the six (6) combined sewer overflow (CSO)outfalls the city currently has active. Each outfall has a drop down menu that details the individual CSO activation time, termination time, and volume of discharge.' (d) 28 river signs at 14 outfalls, in English and Spanish.
notes: Outfalls (permit Attachment F / 2024 Fact Sheet Table 4, DMS lat/long): 011 Schiller St; 018 Turner/Ferry Sts; 031 Stark Brook; 039 Third St (Piscataquog); 043 Tannery Brook; 044 Cemetery Brook; 045 Granite St; 046 Bridge St; 047 Penacook St; 050 MH #1; 051 West Side Pump Station (Piscataquog); 052 MH #2; 053 Walnut/North St Canal/W. Penacook; 054 Ray Brook; 055 Dunbar St. Six outfalls are metered under the Consent Decree; the other nine may be estimated. Permit history: 2025 permit issued 2025-11-03 and appealed (EAB NPDES 25-05). On 2026-09-25 EPA gave notice that all conditions are uncontested and severable and 'will become fully effective and enforceable on November 1, 2026'. The ammonia limit was withdrawn; a draft revision was out for comment 10/01-11/02/2026. The city had contested the 2-hour initial-notice condition before moving to dismiss. Consent Decree (Civ. No. 20-cv-762-SM, entered 2020), paragraph 19(a): 4-hour notice. The FAS notification program went live March 2022 (9-year contract). Under the permit the Public Notification Plan is due 180 days after the effective date and must be implemented within 12 months, so about 2027-11-01 (inferred). Map data comes from ArcGIS Online services owned by 'Greentek' and returns 'Token Required'. Volumes: 2023 875 MG (MRWC); 2024 about half of roughly 896 MG Merrimack-wide (MRWC via NHPR); EPA baseline about 280 MG/yr. Co-permittees Bedford, Goffstown and Londonderry carry the 24-hour public web notice duty for SSOs (Part I.B.2). MRWC notes Manchester does not publish per-event data. All 15 outfalls with decimal coordinates are in the EPA R1 2022 layer (NPDES_ID NH0100447).
